newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shrs to firm on interest cut, eye Reliance.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shrs to firm on interest cut, eye Reliance.

text.p: Bombay blue chips seen opening on a strong note on Thursday following a move by India's central bank to cut interest rates by one percentage point, traders said.
Growing optimism about a favourable bonus share issue to be announced by leading private firm Reliance Industries at its board meeting later today could also firm prices, they said.
"Market expectations have moved up ahead of the Reliance meet," said Vetri Subramaniam, vice-president, equity sales at SSKI Securities Pvt Ltd. "The market should move with Reliance."
Reliance chairman Dhirubhai Ambani is due to address shareholders at the firm's annual meeting at 1100 a.m. (0530 GMT) just after the board of directors meets to finalise the bonus issue.

Rumours of a Reliance bonus issue have grown since the firm's last annual meeting in July 1996 when Ambani told shareholders -- who asked him about a bonus issue -- they would have no cause to complain at the next meeting.
"We could be in for a surprise liberal bonus of one share for every one held," said the head of dealing at a foreign brokeage.
